scenario: [LINT.7.2] and [RLOW.6.1.7]: an operation with two interval operands lowers to FN_INTERVAL_CHECK(s1, e1, s2, e2, v), and with both pairs invalid it yields one fault, chosen as [LNUL.4.2] chooses. I 1 is `5 .. 3` and I 2 is `9 .. 1`. Rule `one_two` tests `(x.a .. x.b) overlaps (y.a .. y.b)` with x the first and y the second, and rule `two_one` the same with the operands swapped; neither fires. Each test is its own node, so each records one ComputationError fault fact ([LERR.9.2]: identity `(node, rule)`), and rule `handler` fires once on each and logs its kind: `DOMAIN`, `DOMAIN`. The two lines are the same, so the order the two handler activations fire in is not pinned, and neither is the `rule`, which for a trap raised during matching is the node's name ([LERR.9.2]). THIS VECTOR PINS THE KIND ONLY. Which pair's start the recorded fault names is LNUL.4.2's within-kind order, which compares the slot context; here both starts are slot `a` of `I`, so only `fact_id`, which the fault fact does not carry, separates the two faults, and schema and slot are not logged. LINT.7.2_two_invalid_intervals_name_the_lower_slot puts the starts in differently named slots and pins which one the fault names. A lowering that guarded only the first pair, or put the check beside `overlaps` in an `and`, would let one rule or both answer false with no fault, and `handler` would log once or not at all. PATH PINNED: the five-argument FN_INTERVAL_CHECK in libds `eval_interval_check` (rete/eval.c) and Mercury `ds.eval.rlow_6_1_7_interval_check`.
rules_ds:
schema I scope logical:
    id: Int key
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable

rule one_two:
    I x where x.id == 1
    I y where y.id == 2 and (x.a .. x.b) overlaps (y.a .. y.b)
->
    log info "one_two"

rule two_one:
    I x where x.id == 1
    I y where y.id == 2 and (y.a .. y.b) overlaps (x.a .. x.b)
->
    log info "two_one"

rule handler:
    ComputationError e
->
    log critical "{e.kind}"
